 now 16.07 EDT 47 min: Ipswich win a throw, then a free kick in short order down the left. Enciso curls the set piece into the mixer. Sels punches powerfully clear under some pressure. The hosts quickly back up to speed.
 Share 51s ago 16.06 EDT 46 min: Philogene hares after a long pass down the left. Forest are very fortunate Milenkovic is immediately switched on; the defender blocks a low cross.
 Share 2m ago 16.04 EDT Ipswich get the second half started. No changes yet.
 Share 9m ago 15.57 EDT Half-time postbag. “There’s always one relegated team per season which is too good to go down. I don’t think it’ll be Forest this season, because they really do look too good to go down, but it could be them if they don’t start putting away their chances. That said, the team too good to go down will probably be Manchester City” – Kári Tulinius.
 “Just to underline how early in the season it still is, the live table has had Forest in 18th, 10th and 17th in the space of half an hour” – Dave Estherby
 “With a clever Austrian manager, a feisty Austrian midfielder (Xaver Schlager) and a crafty Swiss winger (Dan Ndoye), Forest have got a bit of Alpine sturdiness about them these days” – Peter Oh
 Share 14m ago 15.53 EDT The story of first half … told via the medium of mid-80s Scottish indie pop.
 GOAL! Ipswich Town 0-1 Nottingham Forest (Williams 13) GOAL! Ipswich Town 1-1 Nottingham Forest (Enciso 41) Not sure this feature has legs, to be honest.
 Share 18m ago 15.49 EDT HALF TIME: Ipswich Town 1-1 Nottingham Forest
 That was good fun, and the scoreline is about right.
 Share 18m ago 15.48 EDT 45 min +2: Delap literally rips O’Shea’s shirt off his back. O’Shea sporting a racy off-the-shoulder number now.
 Share 20m ago 15.46 EDT 45 min: Enciso romps down the right and swings in low. Emersonn can’t reach the ball before Sels, who snaffles. There will be two additional first-half minutes.
 Share 22m ago 15.45 EDT 43 min: Forest were thinking about a two-goal lead for a few seconds there. But then the ball was turned over, and after one big clanger by Milenkovic, now look! Forest may go all the way back to the Ouattara challenge on Ndoye, but that’s water under the bridge now.
 Share 24m ago 15.43 EDT GOAL! Ipswich Town 1-1 Nottingham Forest (Enciso 41)
 Cunha leads a four-on-two counter but takes a heavy touch. He’s easily dispossessed, and that allows O’Shea to blooter clear. Milenkovic should deal with the ball on halfway, but his attempt to pass back to his keeper is mishit. Underhit. Seriously so. Enciso tears away with it, reaches the edge of the box, and slots past Sels and into the bottom left!
 View image in fullscreen The equaliser. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters View image in fullscreen The home fans are delighted. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  15.48 EDT 26m ago 15.40 EDT 39 min: An Ipswich free kick in a dangerous position, 25 yards out on the right. But Enciso’s delivery is no good, and it’s an easy clearance for Cunha.
 Share 27m ago 15.40 EDT 37 min: Gibbs-White tries to release Ndoye down the inside-left channel, but his team-mate is clumsily brought down by Ouattara. The referee waves play on, much to Forest’s annoyance. Was Ouatarra the last man? Probably not, but that should have been a free kick at the very least.
 Share 29m ago 15.38 EDT 36 min: It’s been a really entertaining match. Very open. No point playing the percentages in this wind.
 Share 31m ago 15.36 EDT 34 min: Walton may have got a little bit on that Gibbs-White bundle, by the way, taking some sting off the ball to make things a bit easier for his team-mate Davis to hack clear. Either way, the Ipswich defence mucked in and got the job done.
 Share 32m ago 15.35 EDT 32 min: … Diop nearly flashes an own goal past Walton. The ball just clears the crossbar. The second corner of the sequence comes in, and Ndoye, facing the wrong way and not obviously aware of what’s going on, sends an unconventional header, let’s say, wide left.
 Share 33m ago 15.33 EDT 31 min: Ndoye barrels into acres down the right. He crosses low and long for Gibbs-White, who slides in and guides the ball back across Walton and the face of goal, towards the bottom right. It’s heading in, but Davis hooks off the line just in time, at the expense of a corner, from which …
 Share 35m ago 15.32 EDT 30 min: Enciso has the ball just to the right of the Forest D. He should release Fatawu into the box with a pass down the inside-right channel, but tries to chop back infield for a shot instead. He’s dispossessed, and the crowd make that sort of noise that most people emit when Ed Sheeran offers to sing.
 Share Updated at  15.37 EDT 37m ago 15.29 EDT 28 min: Enciso dances in from the right and shoots. Straight at Sels. Ipswich are asking questions now.
 Share 37m ago 15.29 EDT 26 min: Ipswich counter and carve out their first big opportunity of the match. A ball swung in from the left. Emersonn takes his second touch of the game, and it’s nearly worthy of an assist. His far-post header’s cushioned back into the path of Philogene, who simply has to score from 12 yards, but bashes his shot straight at Sels, who parries. Forest clear their lines.
 Share 40m ago 15.26 EDT 25 min: Gibbs-White drives down the inside-left channel and upon reaching the edge of the box, uses Diop as a shield while power-curling towards the top right. The shot sails inches wide.
 Share 41m ago 15.25 EDT 23 min: Fatawu advances down the right and looks for Emersonn in the Forest box with a low diagonal. Emersonn can’t get there. He’s only touched the ball once so far, and that to restart the game after the goal.
 Share 42m ago 15.24 EDT 22 min: Munoz once again finds some space down the right. His deep cross is met by Ndoye, but not particularly effectively.
 Share 45m ago 15.22 EDT 21 min: Ipswich pass it around the back for a bit. They’ve done well to settle down after conceding.
 Share 47m ago 15.20 EDT 19 min: Enciso looks for the top-right corner with the free kick. High and wide and not so handsome.
 Share 47m ago 15.20 EDT 18 min: Enciso bursts into some space down the middle and draws a foul out of Gibbs-White and McAtee, who clip him to the floor in a scissor attack. Free kick, in a central position, 25 yards out.
 Share 49m ago 15.18 EDT 17 min: Munoz again makes a nuisance of himself down the right. He feeds Gibbs-White, whose cross is claimed by Walton, but only at the second grab. Forest are getting plenty of joy down this flank.
 Share 50m ago 15.16 EDT 15 min: Delap played his role in that goal as well, winning the first phase of possession, taking down a long pass that gave Munoz something to work with. An absolute belter in the end.
 Share 51m ago 15.15 EDT GOAL! Ipswich Town 0-1 Nottingham Forest (Williams 13)
 This is a lovely goal. Munoz fights for possession down the right, bouncing off O’Shea. The ball breaks to Gibbs-White, who immediately sends Munoz scampering further down the wing. Munoz, in space, swings long for the in-rushing Williams, who cuts in from the left and meets the ball first time, sweeping it powerfully past Walton, who has no chance! Lovely move.
 View image in fullscreen Goal Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen 1-0 to Forest. Photograph: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.24 EDT 55m ago 15.12 EDT 11 min: Both teams are going for it, despite, or perhaps because of, the wind that’s swirling around wildly. It’s been good fun so far.
 Share 1h ago 15.11 EDT 9 min: Fatawu cuts in from the right. He’s got Enciso and Emersonn in the middle, but takes on the shot instead, curling viciously towards the top left. But the shot’s always heading high and wide.
 Share 1h ago 15.09 EDT 8 min: Philogene ships possession carelessly in the centre circle, and suddenly Forest are attacking four on two. Gibbs-White feeds Delap down the inside-right channel; the former Ipswich striker enters the box before slicing a poor shot wide right. Forest looking lively.
 Share 1h ago 15.08 EDT 7 min: Forest win a free kick out on the right. Gibbs-White curls it long. Ndoye wins a header, cushioning down into the path of Cunha, who from the edge of the box pearls a fierce drive towards the top left. Walton parries well. That’ll have warmed his palms.
 Share 1h ago 15.06 EDT 5 min: Philogene drives down the middle of the park. He’s heading down a blind alley, but when he loses the ball it fortunately deflects into the path of Enciso, who has a dig from distance. Miles over the bar.
 Share 1h ago 15.05 EDT 4 min: Munoz hares after a long pass down the right. His cross is calmly dealt with by Diop. Forest first to pretty much everything during these very early exchanges.
 Share 1h ago 15.03 EDT 2 min: It’s windy in Suffolk. Walton batters a clearance upfield as best he can. Forest very much playing with the wind at their back in this first half.
 Share 1h ago 15.02 EDT Most everyone takes the knee … there’s no room for racism … then Forest get the ball rolling. Or flying. Gibbs-White hoicks it straight out for a goal kick.
 Share 1h ago 14.58 EDT The teams are out! Ipswich in blue, Forest in red. A fine Friday-evening post-work, pre-match-pints-fuelled atmosphere at Portman Road. We’ll be off in a couple of minutes!
 Share Updated at  14.59 EDT 1h ago 14.46 EDT Gary O’Neil talks to Sky. “The team today allows us to get more attacking players on the pitch … we want as many as we can … we need to be really secure with the ball … it will be a test … they are a very direct side … a big test of us … one that we can learn a bit more about ourselves and hopefully come out on top.”
 Share 1h ago 14.38 EDT Oliver Glasner speaks to Sky Sports: “When we watch our performances … we feel we could have four, five or six points more … we are doing everything that is necessary to get the win … it is really English weather today! … I expect a very intense game … this is what we have to match … Morgan [Gibbs-White] is maybe the key player in our attack … he is unlucky, he could have five, six, seven assists already … he is very important.”
 Share 2h ago 14.15 EDT Forest start the weekend in 19th place …

 … so is it already time to panic? NOT YET! says Niall McVeigh, who leads off this week’s 10 Things …
 double quotation mark Oliver Glasner … needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers 
 Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend Read more … while it’s a resounding NO! from Will Unwin, who counsels patience.
 double quotation mark Learning the Glasner way is not straightforward … behind the obvious figures, there is plenty of underlying encouragement for Forest 
 Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap Read more Share 2h ago 13.54 EDT Nottingham Forest also make two changes to their starting XI, after their 1-0 loss at home to the champions Arsenal. Morgan Gibbs-White and Nikola Milenković replace Ousmane Diomande, who drops to the bench, and Nicolás Domínguez, who misses out altogether.
 Madueke breaks Nottingham Forest’s resistance as dogged Arsenal edge to victory Read more Share 2h ago 13.52 EDT Ipswich make two changes to their starting XI following their 3-2 defeat at Manchester City last weekend. Abdul Fatawu and Jaden Philogene come in for Jacob Greaves and Daizen Maeda, who drop to the bench.
 Haaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat Ipswich Read more Share 2h ago 13.46 EDT The teams
 Ipswich Town: Walton, Ouattara, Diop, O’Shea, Davis, Palacios, Florentino, Fatawu, Enciso, Philogene-Bidace, Emersonn.
 Subs: Scherpen, Furlong, Matusiwa, Flemming, Greaves, Akpom, Nunez, Maeda, Clarke. 
 Nottingham Forest: Sels, Jair Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo, Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams, Ndoye, Gibbs-White, Delap.
 Subs: John Victor, Diomande, Sangare, Hudson-Odoi, Wood, Kalimuendo, Yates, Netz, Aina. 
 Referee: Thomas Bramall
VAR: Constantine Hatzidakis 
 Share Updated at  14.04 EDT 3h ago 13.30 EDT Preamble
 At last, the 1978 show! That year marking the start of imperial phases for both of these clubs: Ipswich Town won their first and only FA Cup, Nottingham Forest their sole league championship. Within another three years, Town were lifting the Uefa Cup (and really should have won another league title to go with Sir Alf’s heroic flash-in-the-pan) by which point Forest were two-time European champions. A pair of genuinely legendary managers, too, in Bobby Robson and Brian Clough. Glory days colliding, banner moments coinciding. Could it all happen again? Well, there’s no point anyone pulling on their boots if we’re not allowed to dream, so why not? Ipswich can go as high as fifth for the evening, though they’d have to win big, while Forest could catapult themselves into the comfort of mid-table. And after that, a world of possibility stretches out ahead. Bobby and Brian showed us how. Kick-off is at 8pm BST. It’s on!
